provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Cultural masks
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify cultural masks.
The pupils should be able to make their own festival mask.
Introduction:
We see masks during festivals and masquerades.
Today we will learn about Nigerian masks and make one.
Content:
A mask covers the face.
Nigerian masks are used for festivals like Eyo and New Yam festival.
We can use paper plates and colored paper to make masks.
We draw eyes and mouth on the plate.
We add feathers and beads to make it beautiful.
Class activity:
Each pupil will make a cultural mask using paper plates.
They will decorate with colored paper and craft materials.
Evaluation questions:
What is a mask?
Name one Nigerian festival that uses masks.
What materials can we use to make a mask?
Summary:
We learned about cultural masks and made our own festival masks.

topics.title: Dance costume craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make raffia pieces.
The pupils should be able to decorate a dance costume.
Introduction:
We have seen dancers in colorful costumes.
Today we will make parts of dance costumes.
Content:
Dance costumes are special clothes for dancing.
Raffia comes from palm trees.
We cut raffia into long strips.
We tie the raffia to create a skirt.
Beads make costumes shiny and beautiful.
We can make necklaces and bracelets with beads.
Class activity:
Pupils will make raffia skirts using raffia strips.
They will also create bead necklaces for dance costumes.
Evaluation questions:
What is raffia?
What do dancers wear when they perform?
How can we make a costume shiny?
Summary:
We made raffia and bead pieces for dance costumes.

topics.title: Musical instruments
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a simple shaker.
The pupils should be able to play a drum.
Introduction:
We hear music during parties and celebrations.
Today we will make our own musical instruments.
Content:
Musical instruments make sounds.
A shaker makes sound when we shake it.
We can make a shaker with a tin and beans.
A drum makes sound when we hit it.
We can make a drum with an empty can and plastic.
We decorate our instruments with colors and patterns.
Class activity:
Pupils will make shakers using tins and beans.
They will also make drums using empty cans.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does a shaker make?
What materials do we need to make a drum?
How do we play a drum?
Summary:
We made shakers and drums and learned how to play them.

topics.title: Drama props
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a crown.
The pupils should be able to paint a prop.
Introduction:
We see kings and queens wearing crowns in stories.
Today we will make props for our drama.
Content:
Props are things we use in plays.
A crown is a special hat for kings and queens.
We can make a crown with cardboard and foil.
A wand is a stick with a star on top.
We paint scenery to show where the story happens.
We use bright colors to make props attractive.
Class activity:
Pupils will make crowns using cardboard and foil.
They will paint scenery for our drama play.
Evaluation questions:
What is a prop?
Who wears a crown?
What colors should we use for props?
Summary:
We made crowns wands and painted scenery for our drama.

topics.title: Backdrop painting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to paint a stage cloth.
The pupils should be able to work in a team.
Introduction:
We see big pictures behind performers on stage.
Today we will paint the backdrop for our stage.
Content:
A backdrop is a large cloth behind the stage.
It shows the place where the story happens.
We use big pieces of cloth or paper.
We mix colors to make the sky trees and houses.
We paint together as a team.
We share paint brushes and colors.
Class activity:
The class will work together to paint a large stage cloth.
They will paint a scene with sky trees and houses.
Evaluation questions:
What is a backdrop?
Where do we put the backdrop?
How do we paint together?
Summary:
We painted the big stage cloth as a team.

topics.title: Flyer design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design a flyer.
The pupils should be able to write big letters.
Introduction:
We see posters that tell us about events.
Today we will design flyers for our graduation.
Content:
A flyer tells people about an event.
We use bright colors to attract attention.
We write the date time and place of the event.
We use big letters so people can read easily.
We draw pictures related to the event.
We fold the flyer to give to people.
Class activity:
Pupils will design graduation flyers using colored paper.
They will write the details with big bright letters.
Evaluation questions:
What is a flyer?
What information should be on a flyer?
Why do we use big letters?
Summary:
We designed graduation flyers with bright lettering.

topics.title: Photography day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to take a portrait.
The pupils should be able to frame a picture.
Introduction:
We take pictures to remember special moments.
Today we will be photographers and take portraits.
Content:
A portrait is a picture of a person.
We hold the camera steady when we take a picture.
We smile and look at the camera.
We can frame pictures to make them special.
A frame goes around the picture to protect it.
We use colored paper to make frames.
Class activity:
Pupils will take portraits of their friends using toy cameras.
They will frame their best picture with decorated paper.
Evaluation questions:
What is a portrait?
How do we take a good picture?
What is a frame?
Summary:
We took portraits of friends and framed our best shot.

topics.title: Face painting studio
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to paint a simple design.
The pupils should be able to paint safely.
Introduction:
We see people with painted faces at parties.
Today we will learn to paint faces safely.
Content:
Face painting is drawing on the face with special paint.
We use safe paint that does not hurt the eyes.
We draw simple shapes like stars and flowers.
We paint animals like cats and butterflies.
We use different colors to make designs beautiful.
We wash our face after painting.
Class activity:
Pupils will paint simple designs on each other's faces.
They will take turns being the painter and the painted.
Evaluation questions:
Is face paint safe for eyes?
What simple design can we paint?
How do we clean our face after painting?
Summary:
We painted simple designs and had fun being painted.

topics.title: Rehearsal decor
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to dress the stage.
The pupils should be able to add final touches.
Introduction:
The stage needs to look nice for our show.
Today we will decorate the graduation stage.
Content:
Decor makes the stage look beautiful.
We put up curtains to hide the backstage.
We place flowers around the stage.
 We put up signs for the event.
We arrange chairs for the audience.
We make sure everything is in the right place.
Class activity:
Pupils will help dress the graduation stage.
They will add final touches like flowers and signs.
Evaluation questions:
Why do we decorate the stage?
What can we put on the stage?
How do we arrange chairs?
Summary:
We dressed the graduation stage with final decor touches.

topics.title: Graduation gallery and stage
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their art.
The pupils should be able to give a standing ovation.
Introduction:
We have worked hard on our art all term.
Today we will show our work to everyone.
Content:
A gallery shows many artworks.
We hang our pictures on strings or boards.
The stage is where we perform.
We practice walking on the stage.
We stand tall and smile when we perform.
A standing ovation means everyone stands and claps.
Class activity:
The class will have an art walk showing their best works.
They will practice their stage performance and give applause.
Evaluation questions:
What is an art gallery?
How should we stand on stage?
What is a standing ovation?
Summary:
We had our final art walk and stage reveal with applause.
